method_card.title: Friendships and Personal Qualities
method_card.content:
This lesson covers friendship vocabulary, the qualities you look for in a friend, and how to use opinion verbs and the near future tense to talk about spending time together.

FrenchEnglish
un(e) ami(e)a friend
le/la meilleur(e) ami(e)best friend
s'entendre bien avecto get on well with
se disputer avecto argue with
passer du temps avecto spend time with
la confiancetrust
le soutiensupport
fidèleloyal
honnêtehonest
drôlefunny
patient(e)patient
égoïsteselfish
je pense que / je trouve queI think that
à mon avisin my opinion

Near future tense: Use the present tense of aller + infinitive to say what you are going to do. Je vais sortir avec mes amis = I am going to go out with my friends. Nous allons jouer au foot = We are going to play football. This is the most natural way to add a future time frame in spoken and written French.

Opinion verbs: je pense que, je trouve que, à mon avis are followed by a full clause. Example: Je pense que la confiance est très importante dans l'amitié. (I think that trust is very important in friendship.)

Model paragraph: Mon meilleur ami s'appelle Karim. Je m'entends très bien avec lui car il est fidèle et honnête. Il m'écoute toujours quand j'ai un problème. Ce week-end, nous allons jouer au foot ensemble. (My best friend is called Karim. I get on very well with him because he is loyal and honest. He always listens to me when I have a problem. This weekend we are going to play football together.)
steps: Learn the key friendship vocabulary and personal qualities
Master opinion phrases — à mon avis, je pense que, je trouve que
Form the near future tense with aller + infinitive
Combine opinions with reasons using car and parce que

exam_context.frequency: Core topic — appears in every exam series

worked_examples.question: Translate to English: 'Je m'entends bien avec ma copine car elle est drôle.'

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Break it down: Je m'entends bien avec | ma copine | car | elle est drôle.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Je m'entends bien avec = I get on well with. This is a reflexive verb — the pronoun m' is part of the verb structure.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: car = because (same as parce que). elle est drôle = she is funny.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: I get on well with my friend because she is funny.

worked_examples.question: How do you form the near future tense in French?

steps.label: Step 1
steps.content: Take the present tense of aller: je vais, tu vas, il/elle va, nous allons, vous allez, ils/elles vont.

steps.label: Step 2
steps.content: Add the infinitive of the main verb directly after: je vais jouer = I am going to play.

steps.label: Step 3
steps.content: Example: Nous allons aller au cinéma ensemble = We are going to go to the cinema together.

steps.label: Answer
steps.content: Conjugated aller + infinitive: je vais sortir, elle va rencontrer, nous allons jouer.

bronze.question: Match the French friendship vocabulary to the English meaning
Match the French personal qualities to the English meaning
Complete the sentence with the correct form of aller
sentence_parts: sortir avec mes amis et nous

gaps.correct_explain: vais is the je form of aller in the present tense.
entends is correct — je m'entends bien avec = I get on well with.
meilleur = best. Mon meilleur ami = my best (male) friend.

wrong.meilleure: meilleure is feminine — ami is masculine, so use meilleur.

gaps.correct_explain: Any quality adjective works here. fidèle = loyal.

bronze.question: What does 'À mon avis, la chose la plus importante dans l'amitié, c'est la confiance' mean?
options: In my opinion, the most important thing in friendship is trust
In my opinion, friends are the most important thing in life
I think that confidence is important for friends
My best friend thinks trust is very important

bronze.question: Which sentence correctly uses the near future tense?
options: Je vais passer du temps avec mes amis
Je suis passer du temps avec mes amis
J'ai passé du temps avec mes amis
Je passe du temps avec mes amis

bronze.source_text: Mon meilleur ami est fidèle et honnête. Nous allons jouer au foot ce week-end.
model_answers: My best friend is loyal and honest. We are going to play football this weekend.
hints: nous allons = we are going to
jouer au foot = to play football

gold.question: Role Play
gold.scenario: You are at a leisure centre with a French exchange student. They ask you about your friendships.

bullets.prompt: Say who your best friend is and how long you have known them.
bullets.model_answer: Mon meilleur ami s'appelle Théo. On se connaît depuis cinq ans.
bullets.note: s'appeler; depuis + present tense for duration

bullets.prompt: Describe two qualities your best friend has.
bullets.model_answer: Il est très fidèle et honnête. Il m'écoute toujours quand j'ai un problème.
bullets.note: être + adjective; adjectival agreement (fidèle is invariable for gender)

bullets.prompt: Say what you like doing together.
bullets.model_answer: On adore jouer au foot ensemble et on passe beaucoup de temps au parc.
bullets.note: adorer + infinitive; passer du temps avec

bullets.prompt: Say what you are going to do together this weekend.
bullets.model_answer: Ce week-end, nous allons aller au cinéma et manger une pizza.
bullets.note: near future tense: nous allons + infinitive

gaps.correct_explain: aimerais is the je form of the conditional of aimer. J'aimerais que... = I would like that...

wrong.aime: aime is present tense. The English says 'would like', so you need the conditional: aimerais.
wrong.aimerai: aimerai is the simple future. The conditional has -ais, not -ai.

gaps.rule: Present subjunctive — être after aimerais que (Higher)
gaps.correct_explain: soit is the subjunctive of être, required after j'aimerais que. This is a Higher-level structure.

wrong.est: est is the indicative — after aimerais que, French requires the subjunctive: soit.
wrong.serait: serait is the conditional — after que, you need the subjunctive soit.
